facts.text: In surface mining, fatality data identify large haul trucks running over light vehicles or people in front of them, often when starting from rest, as a leading fatal collision situation.
facts.quote: Large haul trucks running over light vehicles or people in front of them, often when starting from rest.

facts.text: Of 13 US haul-truck collision deaths from 2005 to 2021, five involved light vehicles and three involved pedestrians.
facts.quote: Five of the 13 US haul-truck collision deaths (2005 to 2021) involved light vehicles and three involved pedestrians

facts.text: An MSHA analysis covering 2003 to 2017 found that haul-truck collision victims were primarily light vehicle occupants.
facts.quote: the earlier MSHA analysis (2003 to 2017) found victims "primarily light vehicle occupants"

facts.text: Smaller dump trucks and front-end loaders reversing over workers on foot or smaller vehicles accounted for 67% of 22 blind-area deaths from 2000 to 2006.
facts.quote: Smaller dump trucks and front-end loaders reversing over workers on foot or smaller vehicles (67% of 22 blind-area deaths, 2000 to 2006)

facts.text: Haul trucks going through berms or over dump edges are not object collisions, but accounted for the largest group of haul-truck deaths: 33 of 54.
facts.quote: Haul trucks going through berms or over dump edges. These are not object collisions, but they are the largest group of haul-truck deaths (33 of 54).

facts.text: Loss of control was the largest contributing factor in haul-truck berm cases, contributing to nine of 21 cases.
facts.quote: Loss of control was the largest contributing factor among the 21 berm cases (nine)

facts.text: Ten of 12 haul-truck dump-point cases involved an inadequate or absent berm.
facts.quote: ten of the 12 dump-point cases involved an inadequate or absent berm

facts.text: Seven of 12 haul-truck drivers in dump-point cases were unbelted.
facts.quote: seven of the 12 dump-point drivers were unbelted

facts.text: Preventing haul trucks from going through berms or over dump edges may require road-edge, geofence, speed and stability controls in addition to object detection.
facts.quote: This class may require road-edge, geofence, speed and stability controls in addition to object detection.

facts.text: Underground mining deaths and serious injuries include miners struck or pinned by continuous miners, shuttle cars and scoops.
facts.quote: Miners struck or pinned by continuous miners, shuttle cars and scoops

facts.text: Underground mining records report 39 continuous-miner deaths from 1984 to 2015.
facts.quote: 39 continuous-miner deaths (1984 to 2015)

facts.text: Underground mining records report 42 mobile-haulage deaths and 179 nonfatal pinning, crushing and striking accidents from 1984 to 2014.
facts.quote: 42 mobile-haulage deaths and 179 nonfatal pinning, crushing and striking accidents (1984 to 2014)

facts.text: Underground mining production areas have recorded six deaths and 61 lost-time injuries since 2020.
facts.quote: six deaths and 61 lost-time injuries in production areas since 2020

facts.text: Published sources provide much less granular information on serious nonfatal injury than on deaths.
facts.quote: For serious nonfatal injury the published sources are much less granular than for deaths

facts.text: MSHA underground injury figures lack the speed and motion detail needed for braking design.
facts.quote: the MSHA underground figures, for example, come without the speed and motion detail needed for braking design.

facts.text: Construction fatalities include workers on foot struck by trucks or backing equipment, especially at road construction sites.
facts.quote: Workers on foot struck by trucks or backing equipment, above all at road construction sites

facts.text: Construction sources report 131 backing deaths.
facts.quote: 131 backing deaths

facts.text: Struck-by incidents were the most common cause of death in the construction context described for 2005 to 2016.
facts.quote: struck-by the most common cause of death 2005 to 2016

facts.text: Regulator data describe frequent collisions that cause property damage without injury.
facts.quote: Regulator data describe frequent collisions with damage but no injury

facts.text: A secondary report from NSW describes a grader–haul truck collision causing major damage to both machines.
facts.quote: a grader and haul truck collision with "major damage to both machines" (NSW, secondary report)

facts.text: A reported collision against a decline wall severely damaged a light vehicle.
facts.quote: a light vehicle "severely damaged" against a decline wall

facts.text: NSW reported 30 underground coal LHD and personnel-transport collisions in 12 months in 2025.
facts.quote: 30 underground coal LHD and personnel-transport collisions in 12 months (NSW, 2025)

facts.text: Heavy-to-heavy machine contacts in New Zealand in 2017 caused tyre, rim and structural damage and a loader rollover.
facts.quote: tyre, rim and structural damage and a loader rollover in heavy-to-heavy contacts (New Zealand, 2017)

facts.text: HSE notes that many non-injury reversing accidents cause costly damage to vehicles, equipment and premises.
facts.quote: HSE notes that many non-injury reversing accidents cause costly damage to vehicles, equipment and premises

facts.text: Agencies do not publish property-only collision databases containing exposure, repair cost, movement and machine class comparable to fatality data.
facts.quote: agencies do not publish property-only collision databases with exposure, repair cost, movement and machine class comparable to fatality data.

facts.text: No source was found that quantified property-damage cost from collisions.
